summary.one_liner: A Python agent that runs an 8-stage vulnerability-discovery pipeline against a codebase, using many narrow Claude-driven agents, adversarial validation, and a reachability trace gate.
keywords: find security bugs in my repo
summary.what_it_does: The tool runs a fixed pipeline of eight stages (Recon, Hunt, Validate, Gapfill, Dedupe, Trace, Feedback, Report) over a target repository. Recon maps the repo and emits narrowly scoped Hunt tasks, and Hunt agents each examine one attack class, optionally compiling or running PoCs in per-task scratch directories. A separate Validate stage, on a different model, tries to disprove findings, and Trace checks whether attacker-controlled input can reach the flagged sink. Reachable traces feed Feedback, which seeds new hunts for similar patterns. Each stage uses a markdown prompt and a JSON Schema, with a repair turn when output fails validation. Results are stored in SQLite and JSONL, and the Report stage produces a structured report, exported with the audit report command. Options include a cost cap, concurrency limits, scope-notes files, and an optional live-target mode that reproduces findings over HTTP against a given URL.
use_cases: audit a codebase for security vulnerabilities
find command injection or auth bugs in source code
triage likely-exploitable findings and drop unreachable ones
reproduce vulnerabilities against a running test deployment
find unpatched sibling code similar to past security fixes
generate a structured vulnerability report for a repo
how_to_run: claude setup-token  (optional, for headless auth; or use existing claude login)
notable: Eight-stage pipeline where a second model tries to disprove each finding before it is accepted
Reachability trace gate requires attacker-controlled input to reach the sink
Recon mines git history for past security patches and seeds hunts at unpatched sibling files
Works with Claude subscription login, a headless OAuth token, or an LLM gateway such as OpenRouter
Optional live-target mode reproduces findings over real HTTP with network egress limited to the target host and 127.0.0.1
caveats: Hunt agents have Bash access and are not sandboxed at the OS level; the README recommends running in a disposable VM or container
Agents read everything passed via --add-dir, including .env and secrets directories, and outputs are not scrubbed of those reads
Costs can grow quickly on large repos; a --max-cost-usd cap is available but must be set by the user
Non-Claude models through a gateway may not produce schema-compliant output as reliably
